chunks: Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man passing along one of the roads of the Muslims, and his animal strikes a person with its leg, so he said:

He is not liable for what it strikes with its hind leg, but he is liable for what it strikes with its front legs, because its hind leg is behind him if he is riding. But if he is leading his animal, then by the permission of Allah, he controls its front legs and places them wherever he wishes.

key_terms.طَرِيقٍ مِنْ طُرُقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: a public roadway used by Muslims

ai.seo_question: When is a person liable if his animal injures someone on a public road?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding liability when an animal injures a person on a public path. It distinguishes between harm caused by the animal’s hind leg and its front legs, based on the degree of the owner’s practical control over the animal.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5348 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi, who narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) that he was asked about a man passing through one of the paths of the Muslims, and his animal strikes a person with its leg.

Imam (as) said: "He is not liable for what it strikes with its leg, but he is liable for what it strikes with its front legs because its hind leg is behind him if he is riding. However, if he is leading the animal, then by the permission of Allah (swt), he has control over its front legs and can place them wherever he wishes."
